newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Korea Telecom to bid in Nicaragua phone sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Korea Telecom to bid in Nicaragua phone sell-off.

text.p: The South Korean telecommunications firm Korea Telecom will participate in the partial sale of Nicaragua's state telephone company Enitel, a company official said on Friday.

During his visit this week to Central America, South Korean President Kim Young Sam told Nicaraguan officials that Korea Telecom would participate in the October 3 sale, Enitel spokesman Orlando Barrera told Reuters.
"He gave a formal promise to Nicaraguan Vice President Julia Mena that Korea Telecom would participate in the privatization of Enitel," Barrera said.
The sale of 40 percent of Enitel was originally scheduled for July 18, but was pushed back to July 27, then at the last minute postponed until October 3.
Enitel officials said they postponed the sale at the request of bidders who wanted more time to study the company.
Enitel is the first telephone company in Central America to be privatized and its sale is expected to bring in $100 million to $120 million, Enitel President Rolando Rivas said.
Other potential bidders include Telefonica de Espana, GTE International, AT&T, Sprint International, Stet International of Italy, IUSACEL/Bell Atlantic and CTC of Chile.
The Korean president began a tour of Latin American on Monday with stops in Guatemala, Chile, Argentina, Brazil and Peru.
